title: Lab 3 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Bacterial Growth — growth measurement, dilutions, plate counts

questions.prompt: Which growth measurement methods detect only LIVE cells?

options.text: Direct microscopic counts and electronic cell counters
Plate counts (serial dilution, membrane filtration) and metabolic activity
Electronic cell counters and turbidity measurements

questions.explanation: Live cells: serial dilution and membrane filtration plate counts, metabolic activity. Total cells: direct microscopic count, electronic counters, turbidity, dry weight.

why.A: Both of these count total cells (live + dead).
why.D: Both count total cells, not only live cells.

questions.prompt: This instrument measures how cloudy a broth is. What is it, and what does it measure?

options.text: Electronic cell counter — live cells only

questions.explanation: Turbidity measurements use a spectrophotometer and count total cells (live + dead).

why.B: Turbidity can't tell live cells from dead ones — it measures total cells.
why.C: A centrifuge pellets cells for dry weight measurements.
why.D: Electronic counters pass cells past a laser; they count total cells.

questions.prompt: This instrument spins cells into a pellet so the liquid can be removed and the pellet weighed. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Dry weight uses a centrifuge: the liquid is removed and the dry mass of the cell pellet is weighed — total cells.

why.A: Turbidity uses a spectrophotometer, not a centrifuge.
why.C: Metabolic activity measures food use or production of compounds and waste.
why.D: Membrane filtration traps cells on a filter that is placed on agar.

questions.prompt: In this method, cells on a grid are counted under the microscope. It's used for UTIs and CSF (suspected meningitis). What is it?
questions.explanation: Direct microscopic counts examine cells on a grid under the microscope — total cells. Used for UTIs and CSF when meningitis is suspected.

why.A: Membrane filtration grows colonies on a filter placed on agar.
why.C: Plate counts count colonies on agar, not cells on a slide.
why.D: Electronic counters count cells as they block a laser beam.

questions.prompt: A sample is passed through a filter that retains the cells, and the filter is placed on an agar plate. This plate shows the result of:

options.text: Membrane filtration plate count — live cells

questions.explanation: Membrane filtration: the filter retains cells and is transferred to an agar plate. Only live cells form colonies.

why.A: Direct counts are done on a microscope slide.
why.C: Turbidity is read with a spectrophotometer.
why.D: Dry weight uses a centrifuged pellet.

questions.prompt: What number of colonies makes a plate 'countable'?
questions.explanation: A countable plate has about 30–300 colonies; each colony counts as one CFU. Serial dilutions may be needed to get one.

why.B: Fewer than 30 colonies is too few to be reliable.
why.C: More than 300 is too many to count (TMTC).
why.D: Counts must fall in the 30–300 range to be accurate and reliable.

questions.prompt: This plate has far more than 300 colonies. How is it recorded?
questions.explanation: Plates above 300 colonies are TMTC; a more dilute plate is needed for a countable result.

why.C: This plate has too many colonies, not too few.
why.D: A negative control should show no growth.

questions.explanation: Each colony arose from a single live cell, so it counts as one colony forming unit (CFU). CFU/mL = live bacteria per mL of the original sample.

why.A: CFU is a colony counting unit, not a fermentation measure.
why.C: CFU refers to colonies, not filters.
why.D: Colonies are counted; fluorescence isn't involved.

questions.prompt: 1 mL of sample is added to 1 mL of water. What is the dilution factor?
questions.explanation: Dilution factor = volume transferred ÷ total volume after transfer = 1 mL ÷ 2 mL = 1/2.

why.A: The total volume is now 2 mL, so the dilution is 1 of 2.
why.B: 1/10 would come from 1 mL added to 9 mL of water.
why.C: The dilution factor is volume added ÷ total volume: 1 ÷ 2.

questions.prompt: 1 mL of original sample goes into 9 mL of water (Tube A). Then 1 mL of Tube A goes into 9 mL of water (Tube B). What is the total dilution of Tube B?
questions.explanation: Total dilution = Tube A factor × Tube B factor = 1/10 × 1/10 = 1/100.

why.A: 1/10 is only Tube A's dilution factor.
why.C: Dilution factors are multiplied, not added: 1/10 × 1/10.

questions.prompt: Using the same 1 mL into 9 mL series, what is the total dilution of Tube C?
A countable plate from the 1/10,000 total dilution has 34 colonies, and 1 mL was plated. How many CFU/mL were in the original culture?
questions.explanation: CFU/mL = colonies × reciprocal of total dilution ÷ volume plated = 34 × 10,000 ÷ 1 mL = 340,000 CFU/mL.

why.B: Multiply by the reciprocal (10,000), not by 100.
why.C: Use the reciprocal of the dilution (10,000), not the dilution itself.

questions.prompt: In the Sterile Transfer skills assessment, what result after incubation means you PASSED?

options.text: Cloudiness only at the top of the broth

questions.explanation: A loopful of sterile water goes into sterile nutrient broth. No growth = pass; growth = aseptic technique compromised (one more attempt allowed).

why.B: Growth means aseptic technique was compromised.
why.C: No indicator is used; the test is growth vs no growth.

questions.prompt: Which method counts total cells as they block a laser beam, and is used for UTIs and complete blood counts?
questions.explanation: Electronic cell counters are faster and often more accurate than direct counts — used for UTIs and CBCs. They count total cells.

why.B: A spectrophotometer measures turbidity (light passing through a sample).
why.C: Membrane filtration grows live cells on a filter.
why.D: A colony counter helps count colonies on plates.

questions.prompt: Which statement about colony counting is FALSE?

options.text: Mark each colony on the bottom of the plate as you count
Each colony is counted as one CFU
A countable plate has about 30–300 colonies
Colonies that touch or overlap are counted separately
Serial dilutions may be needed to get a countable plate

questions.explanation: If multiple dots touch or overlap, count them as ONE CFU.

why.A: True — mark from the bottom with a sharpie.
why.B: True — each colony is one CFU.
why.E: True — dilutions help get a countable plate.
